> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **55** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **33** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f486e9c1ba5d79c400cf6b0223dd74768461a8b1` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ac2028cab5f42821bd26fa50e520f69d41e573f4` — the merge of head `a085843323063280fd96067d816b6a049cd74acf` into base `f486e9c1ba5d79c400cf6b0223dd74768461a8b1`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ac2028cab5f42821bd26fa50e520f69d41e573f4 && git checkout ac2028cab5f42821bd26fa50e520f69d41e573f4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f486e9c1ba5d79c400cf6b0223dd74768461a8b1 a085843323063280fd96067d816b6a049cd74acf && git checkout -B drift-repro f486e9c1ba5d79c400cf6b0223dd74768461a8b1 && git merge --no-ff a085843323063280fd96067d816b6a049cd74acf

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f486e9c1ba5d79c400cf6b0223dd74768461a8b1
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f486e9c1ba5d79c400cf6b0223dd74768461a8b1` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a085843323063280fd96067d816b6a049cd74acf`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-core/src/protocol-handshake.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/protocol-handshake.test.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-protocol-handshake.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/packages-install-protocol-incompatible.test.ts + packages/metadata-core/src/index.ts (the `export *` that publishes the interface), packages/metadata-core/package.json (`exports`, not private), packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts (the OS_PROTOCOL_INCOMPATIBLE ledger comment, untouched), packages/cli/src/utils/protocol-version-gap.ts and packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/meta.ts (the CLI readers of the diagnostic), packages/cli/test/migrate-meta-protocol-range.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-handshake-install.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.test.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/artifact-forward-conversion.test.ts (every other in-repo assertion on `migrateCommand`), docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md (D1, line 116), scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs (`verifyRuntimeInterfaceOnly`). Prose face outside scope: .changeset/26480-protocol-ahead-upgrade-remedy.md (read for ②, not judged as code).

Inputs read 2026-10-27T07:34Z: card #26480 body and all 3 comments (triage 6434187705, claim 6434943225, os-dev-report 6436225748; the earlier report 6435591073 on #25235 is superseded and was not used), PR #26530 body (the replaced one, updated 2026-10-27T07:29Z), its 7-file list, `git diff origin/main...a0858433` (merge-base d2ca7079b), and the check-runs on the head. No dispatch order and no seat conclusion was fed.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Public TypeScript surface narrowed, declared right.** `ProtocolIncompatibleDiagnostic.migrateCommand` goes `string` to `migrateCommand?: string` (protocol-handshake.ts:96). The interface is published: `packages/metadata-core/src/index.ts:16` re-exports the module, and `@objectstack/metadata-core@18.2.0` is not private with a `.` export. A required output member becoming optional is a narrowing of what a consumer may rely on, so the `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` declaration (execution-duties.md line 106: a narrowing of a published accept set is `Clause-②: no` and owes this record) is the right one. RIGHT.
2. **Wire shape of `error.details` narrowed on both doors, declared right, closed shape kept.** `protocolIncompatibleAnswer` (protocol-handshake.ts:218) spreads `migrateCommand` in only when defined, so `POST /api/v1/packages` and `POST /api/v1/marketplace/install-local` answer four members for an ahead package and five otherwise; the key is absent, never `undefined`. `ProtocolIncompatibleAnswer.details` is still a `Pick` of five named members (the `Pick` carries the optional modifier through), so no spread of the diagnostic reaches the wire and the "closed shape" rule in the docblock still holds. Both doors share the one resolver, so they cannot drift. RIGHT.
3. **Accept set of the handshake unchanged.** `rangeAdmitsMajor` is untouched; nothing that was admitted is refused or vice versa. The refusal's `code` (`OS_PROTOCOL_INCOMPATIBLE`) and `status` (422) do not move, no error code is added, and `error-code-ledger.zod.ts` is not touched, so no path arm and no `Clause-②: yes` arm is hit. RIGHT.
4. **The new branch is correctly bounded by the ruling.** `ahead` is true only when `targetMajor` is non-null and strictly above `runtimeMajor` (protocol-handshake.ts:458). Floor at or below the runtime keeps `objectstack migrate meta --from N`; floor not determinable keeps the bare `objectstack migrate meta`; a `||` union keeps its lowest alternative as the floor, so `'^10 || ^12'` on 11 still prescribes `--from 10` and `'^13 || ^12'` gets no command. This is the triage ruling word for word ("declared floor major above the runtime's"). RIGHT.
5. **The message's `Run:` segment is gone for the ahead case; no reader parses it.** At the head, non-test readers of the diagnostic are: cloud-connection `reportProtocolIncompatibleEntry` (embeds `diagnostic.message`), the runtime artifact boot and service-package rehydrate (embed `message`), the CLI's `checkProtocolVersionGap` (reads `targetMajor`/`runtimeMajor` only and returns null when the declared major is at or above the installed one, so the ahead case never reaches it), and `migrate/meta.ts` (comment only). `git grep migrateCommand` outside tests at the head hits only the changeset, CHANGELOGs, a QA checklist, the spec ledger comment, `build-spec-changes.ts` (its own unrelated literal) and the handshake itself. The PR's "no in-repo code outside tests reads it" is RIGHT. One prose residue, not a defect: the cloud-connection rehydrate line now prints the handshake's "install a build of ID for protocol 18" followed by its own "Install a version of the package built for protocol 18.0.0 (POST ...)". Redundant, consistent, no contract effect.
6. **No other suite in the tree pins an ahead range to `migrateCommand`.** Every pre-existing assertion on the member uses an older floor (cli `--from 16/17` on the running major, metadata-protocol `PROTOCOL_MAJOR - 1`, runtime app-plugin `PROTOCOL_MAJOR - 5`, artifact-forward-conversion `^17` on `18.0.0`). The narrowing breaks none of them. RIGHT (Test Core shards were still running at review time; see ③).
7. **Refusal tests meet the ADR-0112 minimum.** All three new `[#26480]` blocks assert `code` and the 422 status (the runtime block also `error.httpStatus` and `ApiErrorSchema.safeParse`), assert the four-member `details` with `toEqual` (so an `undefined`-valued key would fail), and keep a control that the older-major prescription is byte-identical. RIGHT.
8. **Residual the predicate leaves, flagged by the dev, judged in-ruling.** `declaredFloorMajor` peels the operator, so on an 18 runtime `the greater-than-18 range` (semver: 19 and up, the package IS ahead) has floor 18, is not `ahead`, and still answers `--from 18`; `the less-than-18 range` likewise. The ruling scoped the fix to a floor strictly above the runtime's, so the PR is correct as ruled, but the card's headline ("a package declaring a NEWER protocol major") is not fully discharged for the exclusive-comparator spelling. Carried to ③ as an escalation, not a defect of this diff.
9. **ADR-0087 D1 prose is now conditional in practice.** docs/adr/0087 line 116 promises the structured diagnostic carries "the exact replay command (`objectstack migrate meta --from N`, D3)". For an ahead package there is no chain to replay, so no exact command exists; the diagnostic's own docblock now says so, the ADR does not. Documentation residue on a governed-adjacent doc, not an accept-set change; carried to ③.
10. **ADR-0087 disposition verified on the committed tree.** `not-required (runtime-interface-only packages/metadata-core/src/protocol-handshake.ts#ProtocolIncompatibleDiagnostic)`: the symbol is an exported `interface` (not a Zod projection), the file is not a metadata surface, and no `*.zod.ts` or spec contract imports or mentions it in code (the only code references are a type import in cloud-connection, which the gate does not scan, by design). The changeset body carries no FROM to TO prescription, so the inherited `no-migration-prescription` refusal does not fire. Both `Check Changeset` runs on the head concluded `success`. RIGHT.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/26480-protocol-ahead-upgrade-remedy.md`: `'@objectstack/metadata-core': patch`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` at line start, a **BREAKING** banner, and the ADR-0087 disposition. The PR body carries the same two lines at line start (after `Fixes #26480`). Title `fix(metadata-core)!:` matches the banner.
- Under ruling A (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, "The LEVEL axis"): `Metadata-protocol: none` grades every introduced entry `patch`; the `(narrowing)` arm loses its level coupling and keeps its carriers (the banner and the ADR-0087 disposition), both present. Neither contradiction fires (`narrowed` is not declared; `added` does not sit under `no`). No `authorable-surface/` or `authorable-defaults/` shard moves. `patch` is the level the diff publishes. RIGHT.
- Only `@objectstack/metadata-core` changes behaviour; the `runtime` and `cloud-connection` hunks are comments and tests, so one changeset entry is the right count (dependents are bumped by the changeset tooling, not declared).
- `Clause-②:` line: `no (narrowing)` is the correct reading of this diff. Nothing widens a published accept set or public surface (no new code, no admitted range, no new member); one published output member narrows. lanes/spec.md line 20-21 (a narrowing is a contract face but not Clause-② yes) and execution-duties.md line 106 agree; the dev's measurement on the diff matches mine.
- Served tier: the committed tree holds no `packages/spec/src/**` non-test path and no governed rule text, and the `(narrowing)` arm is declared on both the PR body and the changeset, so the face is `narrowing` and the tier is `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, as this record is served.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none in os-dev-report 6436225748. Nothing to answer.
- **Dev flag (out_of_scope a): exclusive-comparator floors.** `the greater-than-18 range` and `the less-than-18 range` on 18 keep `--from 18`. Answered: outside the ruling as written (6434187705 scopes "a declared floor major above the runtime's"), so not a defect of this PR; the `the greater-than-18 range` spelling is the same operator dead end the card describes, so it is **escalated to the triage seat as a follow-up card**, class (a), low, dedupe words as the dev listed (`OS_PROTOCOL_INCOMPATIBLE`, `declaredFloorMajor`, exclusive comparator, `the greater-than-18 range`, `migrate meta --from 18`). Not blocking.
- **Dev flag (out_of_scope b) and PR acceptance note: the spec ledger comment.** `packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts:763-765` still lists `migrateCommand` among the five `error.details` members. Comment-only, under `packages/spec`, the lane red line of this claim. Answered: correct for the older-major case, incomplete for the ahead case; **escalated to the spec seat** for a one-clause amendment on its next touch of that file, together with the same residue in docs/adr/0087 line 116 (judgment ①9). Not blocking.
- **PR flag: no FROM to TO line in the changeset.** Answered: AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3 asks for the mapping when "removing or renaming anything an author can write (a spec key, an export, a config field)"; this diff removes and renames nothing authorable, it makes one output member of a runtime interface optional. The `runtime-interface-only` disposition inherits the `no-migration-prescription` refusal (`check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` header, lines 155-163), so a prescription would have refused the disposition. The omission is correct.
- **Dogfood battery head.** The `(narrowing)` arm owes a battery pinned to the head (review-checklist.md line 50). The reported battery ran at `17bb14466` (VERDICT command-exit 0, 300 files passed, 2494 tests passed, 0 failures). `git diff --stat 17bb14466 a0858433` on the fetched objects: 1 file, 1 line, `.changeset/26480-protocol-ahead-upgrade-remedy.md` only; the two heads share every code byte. **Flagged for the dispatching seat to rule**: contract-review.md lets a prose-face-only head move carry the original record forward; whether that exception also covers the battery pin is the seat's call before queueing. My reading is that it does, since no byte the battery exercises differs.
- **Check-runs on the head, read 2026-10-27T07:34Z:** every completed non-skipped run concluded `success`, including Lint & Repo Gates, Check Changeset (2 runs: push and pull_request edited), Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected by code changes, Lint PM dispatch-gates, Type Check source gates and debt ledger, Plan Test Core shards, and the four PR-claim guards (each twice). No run failed. **Still running at review time:** Build Core, Test Core 1/8 through 8/8, Type Check consumer gates, Type Check workspace. The queue's "all checks green" floor (contract-review.md, landing item ②) is therefore not yet readable on this head; the seat reads them before queueing. This verdict rests on the diff and the completed gates and is not contingent on the shards beyond ①6.
- Author: PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no relay login to name.
- Independence: the diff was produced on the card thread's branch; this record was rendered by an isolated subagent that read neither the dispatch order nor the seat's conclusions.
